newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast prods notionally flat in idle market.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast prods notionally flat in idle market.

text.p: Spot barrels of U.S. West Coast products were notionally unchanged with most players out of the market Friday for an industry function, brokers said.
Brokers said they were unsure where prices stood early, with the NYMEX down sharply but PADD 5 West Coast supplies seen tight.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) reported Tuesday that West Coast gasoline fell 554,000 barrels last week.
"We've got a NYMEX that is fairly weak. Without any bids or offers it's hard to say," what price levels are," one broker said.
Refineries, including Mobil, Ultramar and Unocal, were rumored to bid for barrels ahead of today's deadline for March shipments on the Santa Fe Pipeline, traders said.
One trader late Thursday said Exxon's 128,000 barrel-per-day refinery in northern California began the process of restarting several units and was expected to be completely on line by mid-March.
CARB gasoline in Los Angeles were unchanged from Thursday's market at 74/75 cents, after a deal was struck late yesterday at 74.50 cents.
Offers for conventioal L.A. gasoline remained 71 cents.
San Francisco CARB gasoline was done late yesterday at 71.50 cents, and was talked at the same level today, traders said.
